minutes.headline: Committee approved the new grade 8 team model, closed summer extended day, and lifted the hiring freeze for three posts.
minutes.summary: The School Committee met remotely and honored retirees with a video. It approved a restructured eighth grade with an accelerated algebra pilot, declared surplus items, and closed the summer extended day program because of COVID guidelines. It lifted the hiring freeze for three posts, heard a COVID expense update and a Finance Committee report, and went into executive session for union negotiations.

what_happened.line: The School Committee approved a restructured eighth grade, including an accelerated algebra pilot, on a roll call vote with all yes votes heard.
The committee voted to not run the extended day summer camp in summer 2020, citing COVID guidelines.
The committee temporarily lifted the hiring freeze for three positions: a technology post, a student custodian post and long-term substitutes.
The committee declared listed items surplus, which may be auctioned online with any revenue going to the general fund.
The committee accepted senior lunch balance donations, with one abstention, and deferred the choice of distribution to the next meeting.

why_it_matters: The eighth grade change, the summer program closure and the hiring exemptions affect what students and families can expect from the schools in the coming year.
A Finance Committee member raised whether the FY21 long-term substitute budget is enough once the salary reserve is removed, which bears on school costs and the town budget, mostly taxes.
watch_next: June 16 feedback forum and the June 17 meeting, where the Student Opportunity Act plan is due in final draft.
Next meeting: the committee's decision on how to distribute the senior lunch balance donations.
